text:
Jamie Benn reached 1,000 career points on Saturday with the go-ahead goal against Buffalo, only the second fifth-round pick ever to get there, and he did it in the only NHL sweater he has worn. The Stars followed it with an overtime win over Florida on Jason Robertson's goal, which makes for a neat bit of symmetry: the franchise's past and the player whose future is being argued about everywhere. Robertson has been in trade-rumor headlines all month, including one insider floating a Robertson for Nikita Kucherov deal, and one analyst calling it "difficult to imagine" him signing long term in Dallas. None of that is a move. It is a lot of noise around a player who just won a game.

Dallas may also get Miro Heiskanen back. He has missed five straight games and is now off the out list and day-to-day. The Stars have been the slightly better five-on-five team this season (53% of the expected goals, the share of chance quality), and Jake Oettinger is 7.8 goals saved above expected. The habit that costs them is the penalty box: 4.1 minors a game against 3.2 drawn.

Vegas is stinging. The Golden Knights lost 6-3 at home to a Vancouver team that had gone 0-7-0, and Mark Stone did not dress it up. Asked by The Athletic's Jesse Granger whether they overlooked the opponent, he said, "The result for sure shows that. I don't think we managed momentum very well." The Knights still won the chance battle that night, as they have in four of their last five.

There is plenty of form on their side. Victor Olofsson has 11 points in nine games with chances to match, Tomas Hertl has a seven-game point streak, and Mitch Marner, with a ten-game home point streak, needs one assist for 600. Adin Hill is .930 over his last five starts after a rough 2025-26. Noah Hanifin is out. Our numbers have it tight: 2.99 expected goals for Vegas, 2.81 for Dallas.
headline: Benn's 1,000 behind him, Robertson's future ahead
